subject: Private deploy: hop-by-hop latency analysis & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@datapulse.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iy@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Private deploy: hop-by-hop latency analysis & next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — good alignment on the end-to-end goals. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can validate whether your on-prem/VPC path will meet the streaming & concurrency expectations for the pilot.

Goals we heard (restating):
- Streaming tail budget: p99 per-chunk latency < 200 ms (target), p95 < 120 ms for 1 KB tokens
- Interactive generation: p95 token latency < 60 ms for single-stream low-latency routes
- Throughput/concurrency: sustain 600 concurrent streaming connections (~3K tokens/s aggregate) with graceful degradation above 1K concurrent
- Recovery/fallback: <5s failover to secondary peering region for session reattach

Summary of technical constraints you called out:
- Traffic will egress from your VPC via a Transit Gateway into our peering (IPsec) to a colo in us-east-1
- MTU is standard (1500) but there are intermediate NAT boxes and a custom firewall enforced by the infra team
- You're currently using BGP over IPsec with ECMP across two tunnels

Immediate validation tasks (owners & timing):
1) Traceroute + per-hop latency sweep (DataPulse ops) — run from an app host in the VPC to 3 Redwood ingress IPs during your normal business hour window. Output CSV + raw traceroutes. (owner: Alex, due: 2026-11-18 EOD)
2) iperf3 burst and sustained runs to measure TCP handoffs and throughput under 150/300/600 concurrent simulated streams (DataPulse + Redwood ops). Collect pcap for failing cases. (owner: DataPulse ops + Karthik, schedule: 2026-11-19 02:00–03:30 UTC)
3) MTU and MSS verification, and confirm NAT timeouts and TCP keepalive settings used by your load balancer (owner: Alex, due: 2026-11-19 noon PT)
4) Redwood to instrument a streaming sender test to replicate chunking and KV cache behavior at 1 KB chunk sizes, measure p50/p95/p99 token latencies end-to-end (owner: Karthik, deliverable: test harness link + results, due: 2026-11-19 end-of-day)

Attach: empty traceroute template (CSV) and the test plan we walked through.

Key acceptance criteria for pilot cutover:
- p95 streaming chunk latency across gateway < 200 ms for typical payloads
- No packet loss >0.5% on 10-minute windows during sustained concurrency runs
- Failover < 5s to secondary peering without session data loss (if we cannot fully validate, we want a rollback plan)

Please confirm owners and times. If any of the above looks off, call it out and we will adapt. I can run the Redwood side of the iperf+stream harness; Karthik will coordinate the test harness and quantify model-side token timing.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.ch@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: 20261118-traceroute-aggregates.csv (template), private-deploy-test-plan.pdf (inline link)

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@datapulse.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@datapulse.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:02:14 -0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy: hop-by-hop latency analysis & next steps

Thanks, Irene — appreciated the clear checklist. Confirming owners:
- Traceroute + CSV: I'll run and upload by EOD (we'll capture 30-minute samples over our peak and off-peak).
- MTU/MSS & NAT timeouts: I will get the exact LB config and NAT timeout settings from infra (ETA midday tomorrow).

Couple of clarifications and notes from our infra lead:
- We have two IPsec tunnels via Transit GW to the colo; both advertise the same prefixes. We do observe asymmetric paths for some routes (likely ECMP).
- Our current TCP keepalive is 2 hours; we can tighten to 5 minutes for the test window if that helps streaming stability.
- We cannot run iperf during peak traffic but can run at 02:00–03:00 UTC as proposed — that window is fine.

One ask from our side: can Redwood provide a light-weight client that mimics your chunked streaming (1 KB chunks, 20ms inter-chunk pacing) and a small harness to measure token latencies per chunk including TLS handshake time? If so, we can run it from our app hosts and collect results without injecting synthetic application traffic.

I'll upload the traceroute CSV to the shared Drive link and ping you when it's there.

— Alex
Alex Moreno
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, DataPulse
alex.moreno@datapulse.com

Attachment stubs: none (will attach traceroute CSV once run)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iy@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@datapulse.com>, Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy: hop-by-hop latency analysis & next steps

Alex — thanks for the quick response. We do have a small streaming test client (node + go variants) that reproduces chunking, incremental TLS writes, and KV cache stickiness. I can drop a package and a runbook into the Drive link by 2026-11-18 18:00 UTC. That harness will:
- open N concurrent TLS streams (configurable)
- send configurable 1 KB chunks at X ms pacing
- log per-chunk send/ack timestamps and any TLS renegotiation events
- emit a summary with p50/p95/p99 for chunk RTT and token generation time (approx)

For the acceptance criteria, to be pragmatic given BGP/ECMP asymmetry, propose we:
- target p95 < 220 ms for initial pilot, with a follow-up optimization window to bring it under 200 ms after routing tweaks;
- require p99 < 400 ms for the pilot (we'll instrument and show regression alerts if p99 > 400 ms during test windows)

Action items I will take:
- Drop the harness + runbook into the Drive link (owner: Karthik) — 2026-11-18 18:00 UTC
- Coordinate with Irene to run the Redwood sender from our side for one daylight window post-traceroute results

If DataPulse can tighten keepalives to 5 minutes just for the test window, that will reduce session tear behavior we sometimes see when NATs close idle flows. Also, please confirm whether the Transit GW preserves DSCP for priority — we rely on QoS tagging on some customer paths.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iy@redwood.ai

Attachments: none

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@datapulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iy@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:05:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy: hop-by-hop latency analysis & next steps

Quick update: uploaded traceroute CSV (20261118-traceroute-aggregates.csv) to the Drive link and scheduled the iperf window for 2026-11-19 02:15–03:15 UTC.

Findings from a quick look:
- Average hop latency to primary colo egress ~18 ms per hop for first 3 hops, then a 60 ms hop across the regional transit. We see an infrequent 200–300 ms spike on one of the AS paths at 1:32 UTC (likely a transit provider transient).
- NAT timeout config: 15 minutes (we can change to 5 minutes for test window)
- DSCP: preserved through our Transit GW, but last-mile provider strips some markings (we'll include a note in the CSV)

We'll run the iperf + harness as agreed and attach the pcap if we hit retransmit/large jitter events. I will also confirm GRE vs IPsec specifics — looks like IPsec (AES-GCM) with BGP.

See you in the test window.

— Alex
Alex Moreno
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, DataPulse
alex.moreno@datapulse.com

Attachments: iperf-schedule.txt, 20261118-traceroute-aggregates.csv, iperf-notes.txt
